title: Skipping a fixed head literal in the term sub-tree
statement: Let $\rho$ be a restriction on $n$ variables and $g$ a continuation assigning a decision tree to each restriction on $n$ variables. Fix a variable $v$, a Boolean value $b$, and a literal $\ell$ whose variable is $v$, and let $\mathit{rest}$ be a further list of literals. Write $\rho[v \mapsto b]$ for the restriction that agrees with $\rho$ everywhere except at $v$, where it is fixed to the value $b$. Then the term sub-tree built from the list obtained by prepending $\ell$ to $\mathit{rest}$, under $\rho[v \mapsto b]$ with continuation $g$, coincides with the term sub-tree built from $\mathit{rest}$ alone under the same restriction and the same continuation.
hypotheses_covered: the head literal $\ell$ queries the variable $v$ (its variable equals $v$)
the restriction is updated at $v$ to fix it to the value $b$
replaced:
If $l.\mathrm{var} = v$, then $\mathrm{termSubTree}\,(l :: \mathit{rest})\,(\rho[v \mapsto b])\,\mathrm{cont} = \mathrm{termSubTree}\,\mathit{rest}\,(\rho[v \mapsto b])\,\mathrm{cont}$,
since after the update $v$ is no longer free and $l$ is skipped.
